verses.english: Linked Discourses 7.7
1. The Perfected Ones
With Bhāradvāja the Pure
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Atha kho suddhikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Pure went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side,

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho suddhikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: and spoke this verse in his presence:
“No brahmin in the world is ever purified
even though he’s ethical and mortifies himself.
But one accomplished in knowledge and conduct

verses.pali: So sujjhati na aññā itarā pajā”ti.
verses.english: is purified, not these other commoners.”
“Even one who mutters many prayers
is no brahmin by birth
if they’re filthy and corrupt within,
supporting themselves by fawning.
Regardless of whether you’re an aristocrat,
a brahmin, peasant, menial, <j>or a corpse-worker or scavenger—
if you’re energetic and resolute,
always staunchly vigorous,
you’ll attain ultimate purity.
Know that for a fact, brahmin.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, suddhikabhāradvājo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he had spoken, the brahmin Bhāradvāja the Pure said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama …” …

verses.pali: aññataro ca panāyasmā bhāradvājo arahataṁ ahosīti.
verses.english: And Venerable Bhāradvāja became one of the perfected.
